root_cause_criterion.criterion: When xmlTextReaderRemoveID transfers the attribute-name buffer into the xmlID record, it must clear `attr->name` before returning so later attribute cleanup does not free that transferred buffer while the ID table still owns it.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original leaves `attr->name` pointing at the transferred `"id"` heap buffer after `id->name = attr->name`, so the attribute node and the xmlID record still share ownership. The fixed original nulls `attr->name`, leaving the transferred buffer owned only by `id->name`.

nodes.state: Property cleanup reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` and frees the same transferred attribute-name buffer that `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` left live in the xmlID record.
xmlFreeID reaches `DICT_FREE(id->name)` on the stale xmlID record entry and becomes the AddressSanitizer-reported second free.

edges.relation: The pointer transferred into `id->name` at xmlTextReaderRemoveID is the same heap name pointer later freed through `cur->name` during attribute cleanup.
After attribute cleanup frees the transferred name buffer through `cur->name`, ID-table teardown later reaches `xmlFreeID` and frees that same pointer again through `id->name`.
